John Pilger: Why the rise of fascism is again the issue

Pilger does a pretty good job of debunking the propaganda myth that the American Empire's wars are entered into reluctantly, and for defensive purposes. While the Western media portrays every designated enemy of the month as "the next Hitler" and "the greatest threat to the world since World War II", the truth is that the United States is the one following the path taken by Germany in the last century. The US is by far the most aggressive and dangerous regime in the world today.

As a leftist, Pilger predictably misconstrues the motives behind American aggression somewhat, and his view of the benevolence of socialist governments like Venezuela's is quite deluded. But he's right about the West, and in particular about the complicity of the media in the rise of the new fascism.

Fascism is preserved as history, as flickering footage of goose-stepping blackshirts, their criminality terrible and clear. Yet in the same liberal[sic] societies, whose war-making elites urge us never to forget, the accelerating danger of a modern kind of fascism is suppressed; for it is their fascism.

Many have said that America is sleepwalking towards fascism. I don't think that's true. Fascism is already here. People don't recognize it because it doesn't come with the goose-stepping, the black uniforms, and most of all, the one-party states - but none of those things were essentials - not even the antipathy to democracy. Fascism in Italy and Nazism in Germany were both popular mass movements. They opposed democracy because democracy was widely regarded as discredited in those countries at that time.

So what is essential to fascism? In the words of Benito Mussolini, the creator of fascism:

The keystone of the Fascist doctrine is its conception of the State, of its essence, its functions, and its aims. For Fascism the State is absolute, individuals and groups relative.

and again:

All within the state, nothing outside the state, nothing against the state.

This means that under fascism, the state's control pervades all of society. The distinction between state agencies and private organizations dissolves; there is no sphere of private life free in principle from state regulation; no individual rights are upheld against the interests of the state. The glorification of war was another essential feature of fascism:

War alone brings up to their highest tension all human energies and imposes the stamp of nobility upon the peoples who have the courage to make it.

Now, which of these essential elements of fascism is not endemic in America today? The Bill of Rights is essentially a dead letter. The government claims (and to a great extent exercises) the right to regulate every aspect of people's lives. The courts throw out legally sound cases on the pretext that enforcing the law would threaten "national security". The big corporations are inseparably entangled with the government. The media disseminates propaganda. Virtual worship of the military is considered normal.
